task: Verify every recovered ZolikaPatch option signature against the real game, per option
method: For every option in evidence/option_signatures.json each signature is parsed with the exact semantics of tools/verify_game_signatures.py (whitespace-split tokens; '?'/'??' wildcards; otherwise strtoul-hex low byte) and matched with find_all over the raw .text bytes of the read-only GTAIV.exe. The image is never modified. An option RESOLVES if ANY of its signatures has >=1 hit. Per-signature hit_count and first RVA are recorded. The recovered build gate (evidence/option_build_gates.json) is then cross-referenced for build v1080 (ordinal 9) with the same gate semantics as evidence/verify_ops_vs_game.json: gated-in for ordinal 9 iff no '!=' gate names 9 and (no '==' gate exists or some '==' gate names 9).

inputs.tool: tools/verify_game_signatures.py::verify (re-run; per-signature hits and RVAs agree 100%)

summary.agreement_with_game_verification_json: same three unresolved options (RemoveRGSCLoginRequirement, VRAMFix, VSyncFix)

gate_cross_check.semantics: gated-in for ordinal 9 iff no '!=' gate names 9 and (no '==' gate or some '==' gate names 9)

exceptions.explanation: Handler FUN_10045490 first pattern-scans the single recovered signature. In GTAIV.exe 1.0.8.0 the scan fails (hit_count 0) because the matched routine's prologue differs from the signature's first ~15 tokens. The decompiled handler explicitly handles this case: when the scan returns null AND DAT_1015be04 == 9, it patches the module-relative RVA 0x498460 instead (VirtualProtect @ image_base+RVA 0x498460, writes 0xE9). That RVA is inside .text (VA 0x898460) and the bytes there (8B 44 24 04 85 C0 74 17 F3 0F 7E 05 30 A4 D8 00) are a plausible function entry preceded by CC padding, so the leading byte 0x8B is the byte that would be overwritten. The option therefore still applies on build 9 through the recovered RVA fallback op (verify_ops_vs_game.json rva op #58, gate_applicable_to_1080=true), not through a signature. This is a designed per-build fallback, not an extraction defect.
exceptions.cross_reference: evidence/fallback_patch_sites.json (same finding, same bytes); evidence/verify_ops_vs_game.json anomalies.flagged type signature_absent_gate_includes_1080 (handler 10045490).

exceptions.type: unresolved signature with no recovered build gate
exceptions.explanation: Handler FUN_1004aae0 has no DAT_1015be04 comparison, so no build gate was recovered and the signature is expected to hold for every build. The single signature '8B 44 24 10 D9 2C 24 83 C4 1C C3' is absent from the 1.0.8.0 .text. Near-miss diagnostic: the longest matching prefix is only 5 tokens ('8B 44 24 10 D9'), with 54 prefix hits scattered across the image and no full-length match, i.e. the trailing epilogue '83 C4 1C C3' is not anchored by the recovered prefix in this build. FusionFix resolves VRAM detection through a different mechanism (memory.ixx GetProcessPreferredGPUMemory, pattern 8B 0D ? ? ? ? 83 EC ? 33 C0), so no independent confirmation exists. Recorded UNRESOLVED: treated as a build-variant signature (the exact routine text differs in 1.0.8.0); no positive build gate and no RVA fallback was recovered, so resolution cannot be asserted.

exceptions.type: unresolved signature, resolved (absent) by recovered build gate
exceptions.explanation: Gate semantics: '!=' 9 is present, so the handler body (FUN_100503b0, which pattern-scans and rewrites an indirect call target per build) is skipped entirely for build ordinal 9. The two signatures are therefore expected to be absent on 1.0.8.0 and their non-resolution is consistent, not an extraction defect. Both signatures have 0 hits; longest matching prefixes are 11/12 and 18/27 tokens respectively, i.e. the neighbouring code is present but the exact per-build variant differs. No RVA fallback op exists for this option.

Gate-semantics false positive. FUN_10006770 pattern-scans '8B 17 8B 42 64 8B CF FF D0 8B 54' UNCONDITIONALLY (the FUN_10003830 call is outside any DAT_1015be04 branch) and only the injected trampoline target is chosen per build: BuildSlot in {1..6} -> LAB_10006630, else -> LAB_100064F0. The ==1..==6 gate therefore encodes trampoline-target selection, not option applicability. Presence in 1.0.8.0 .text is expected; the signature resolves uniquely at RVA 0x4f7ce5 (VA 0x8f7ce5), matching docs/handlers_batch_1.md. The hook is still installed on build 9 with the else-branch target.

uncertainties: Build gates are a heuristic extraction; positive '==' gates are reliable but negative '!=' gates can encode branch/target selection rather than applicability (demonstrated by DualVehicleHeadlights).
VRAMFix remains genuinely unresolved: no positive gate, no RVA fallback, no independent FusionFix site. It is recorded as unresolved rather than as a defect.

RemoveRGSCLoginRequirement's signature absence is explained by a recovered RVA fallback, but the fallback target (RVA 0x498460) was not proven to be the same routine the signature describes: the leading 0x8B at that RVA is consistent with a function entry preceded by CC padding, and the surrounding bytes are plausible, yet no byte-level identity proof was produced.
